description.narrative: This programme will support the Addis Ababa City Administration (AACA) to implement the Sheger Project using a holistic approach of nesting integrated watershed management within the broader ambit of sustainable urban land use planning

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

1. Establish frameworks, including institutional structure and systems that leverage digital technologies and big data for (e) urban development using smart technologies. 1.1 Application of smart technologies on paper less/ICT based management is piloted in Mega Projects Construction Office. Towards this end, Addis Ababa University Institute of Information and Technology is contracted to assess organizational setup and develop System Requirement Specifications for the office. 1.2 Paper free/ICT based office administration system is designed in collaboration with Ethiopian Defense Enterprise for Mega Projects Construction Office. Moreover, High-Capacity server, computers and laptops are procured for the office that are used to run the system. The system is now on pilot phase. 1.3 Series of trainings are arranged to more than 50 staff of Mega Projects Construction office on electronic records keeping and application of the system. 1.4 Training of Trainers on GIS, GPS, Remote Sensing and GPR application on infrastructure integration and management is provided to 25 (20% women) trainees drawn from 20 institutions of Addis Ababa City responsible for infrastructure development and management including urban greenery. This practical training was arranged for 25 days in collaboration with Ethiopia Space Science and Geospatial Institute and Adama Science and Technology University. 2. Develop (a) stakeholder engagement plan; (b) gender action plan; (c) heritage rescue and management plan; (d) resettlement action plan formulated and approved by AACA. 2.1 Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) has been conducted on the whole project area of river side development. Based on the findings of the study, Resettlement Action Plan Framework is developed according to national and international experiences and guidelines. 2.2 Map of tourist attraction sites including heritage sites is developed in collaboration with Ethiopian Tourism and Catering Training Institute. Moreover, general management guideline is developed for the heritage sites. 3. Creating women-led Common Interest Groups and link with microfinance institutions/CIGs Savings Groups 3.1 Natural Resource Valuation guideline is developed by a consultant for recording natural capital and ecosystem accounts in Addis Ababa. Training is provided to experts of different responsible organizations on the guideline. 3.2 In-depth Analysis on Livelihood and Sustainable Options for people living along the Beautifying Shger project area was conducted by a consultant. Moreover, business opportunities close to tourist attraction sites was conducted by Tourism and Catering Training Institute. 3.3 Based on the findings of the livelihood study, the project has supported project affected people to sustainably restore their livelihood. In this regard, Entrepreneurship Development Center (EDC) and Tourism and Catering Training Institute were contracted to train more than 1,400 women and youth on Entrepreneurship, business management, catering and tourist guiding.
